ink-subtle.purpose: Third-tier text: quiet chrome and secondary metadata.

ink-on-pastel.purpose: The one text ink used on tinted status grounds.

success-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.04 152). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.13 152).

warning-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.05 60). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(55% 0.16 60) — a darker, more saturated base than the foreground hue, struck so the lamplit plate does not wash out.

error-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.04 25). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.18 25) — same reasoning as the warning ground.

info-bg.purpose: Light: flat pastel at oklch(96% 0.03 245). Dark: 22% in-oklab mix of oklch(50% 0.14 245).

display.purpose: Masthead wordmark and homepage hero only.

headline.purpose: Page titles (h1), opened by a 2px ink rule; steps down to the --text-3xl clamp below 768px.

subhead.purpose: Section headings (h2); 1.875rem below 768px. Never painted in primary.

title.purpose: h3 and ledger-row item titles; 1.875rem at >=768px. In-record block heads drop to 1.1875rem at weight 700.

body-serif.purpose: Article full text and ledes at 44-52.5rem measures, line-height 1.7.

label.purpose: Datelines, metadata labels, chips, disclosure toggles, nav strip; 11px (--text-2xs) is the absolute floor.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Modals; rare. Dark is struck from pure black at higher alpha and greater spread — a neutral-ink shadow is invisible on a lamplit ground.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: THE default focus indicator, paired with outline-offset: 2px.

shadows.name: ring-focus
shadows.purpose: Box-shadow focus ring — the exception, for controls an outline would be clipped on. Also the input focus ring, paired with a primary border.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: Larger reveals; ceiling. No bounce, no elastic.

typeMap.purpose: Fixed semantic map for resource types and entities, rendered as dots on outlined chips. Declared in BOTH theme blocks: as :root-only aliases they inherited already-substituted light hues under the data-theme toggle.

categoricalSeries.purpose: The theme-owned categorical chart palette, consumed by IwacVisualizations. Slots 1-2 alias --primary/--secondary and flip with the theme; slots 3-20 are literals held at parity across themes. Slots 4 and 8 were lifted out of the crossover band so knocked-out labels stay legible.

narrative.overview:
A 20th-century broadsheet operated as a scientific instrument. The site is a scholarly database — LLM sentiment models, LDA topics, embeddings, IIIF — that carries the visual grammar of the newspapers it preserves: masthead wordmark, uppercase section strip, thick 2px ink rules, datelines, ledger-style result rows, a duotone press-collage hero. The execution is a modern broadsheet's digital archive run by a university press: newspaper typographic conventions with Linear/Stripe-grade product polish.

Density is a feature, not a compromise: researchers want more items per screen, flat ledger rows over boxed cards, metadata flowing inline with interpunct separators. Restraint is the resting state — the quiet control is the default and loudness opts in. Confirmed anti-references: not a small museum's website, not a warm editorial magazine, not a generic dashboard; no cream or parchment, no pastiche of aged paper.

The system is enforced, not merely written down. Every value the token generator publishes is compared by a guard in this repo and in both consumer modules; a rule that lives only in prose is a rule that has already drifted. That doctrine — publish it and assert it — is why the palette below includes the twenty categorical chart slots and the nine resource-type hues that once lived as loose hex in a sibling repo.
keyCharacteristics: Newspaper grammar (rules, datelines, ledgers) executed with product-grade polish
Density over comfort; typography as architecture, rules as joinery
Near-white cool-neutral light mode; warm "lamplit reading room" dark mode
One brand accent used sparingly; category encoded as dots, never fills
Two themes declared in full — dark is a redeclaration, never an inherited substitution

rules.name: The One Plate Rule
rules.body: The duotone hero — a grayscale collage multiplied over a primary ground — is the one big color statement on the site. Everything else earns primary only as an accent.

rules.name: The Dot-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Category is a dot on an outlined chip, never a filled or pastel badge. Ten filled badges per screen is shouting; ten dots is an index.

rules.name: The Data-Only Secondary Rule
rules.body: #394f68 exists for data. If it appears on a button, link, or focus ring, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Redeclare-In-Dark Rule
rules.body: A token whose value contains `var(…)` must be declared in the dark block too. Declared once on `:root`, it is substituted against light referents and inherited frozen by every dark descendant — a whole-theme failure that looks like nothing until a contrast probe finds it.

rules.name: The Published Scale Rule
rules.body: A color that encodes data belongs in `tokens.json` with a name, a light value and a dark value. Owning a scale means deciding it, never leaving it unpublished in a consumer's source.

rules.name: The Slab Tracking Rule
rules.body: Besley display sizes track at -0.01em, never the full -0.02em — slab serifs clog at tight tracking.

rules.name: The Lining Zero Rule
rules.body: Besley's `tnum` zero is broken (frozen at 55 units across weights); use `font-feature-settings: "lnum"` for aligned numerals, never `tabular-nums` with the display serif. All headings set `"kern" "liga" "dlig" "lnum"`.

rules.name: The No-14px Rule
rules.body: The type scale deliberately skips 14px; 11px (`--text-2xs`) is the floor. Absolute `font-size` literals fail `npm run check:tokens` — use `--text-*` tokens.

rules.name: The Bound Punctuation Rule
rules.body: French sets a space before `: ; ! ?` and `»` and after `«`. Rendered as an ordinary space it is a legal line-break opportunity, and a headline can open a line with an orphaned colon that reads as a bullet. Titles pass through the `FrenchSpacing` helper, which rewrites those spaces to U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE — same gap, no break.

rules.name: The Separator-Ends-The-Line Rule
rules.body: An inline separator between repeated values is drawn with `::after` on the preceding value, never `::before` on the following one. Each value is an atomic wrap unit, so a leading separator opens whichever line its box starts — an interpunct that reads as a bullet.

rules.name: The Glass Once Rule
rules.body: Backdrop-filter belongs to the sticky header and nowhere else.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Boxes Rule
rules.body: Before adding a shadowed card, try a 2px ink rule or a hairline. Boxes are a last resort for true panels. The AI lede, the linked-resources filter bar, and the transcript disclosure were all boxes once and are all rules now.

rules.name: The Outline-First Focus Rule
rules.body: `--focus-outline` at 2px offset is the focus indicator. The `--ring-focus` halo is the exception for clipped or oddly-shaped controls, never the default — it is the weaker indicator, and reaching for it by habit is how a surface ends up with no visible focus at all.

dos: **Do** open sections with 2px ink rules and divide rows with hairlines — typography is the architecture, rules are the joinery.
**Do** declare every composed or aliased token in the dark block as well as the light one, so dark pages compose against dark referents.
**Do** publish any color that encodes data as a named light/dark pair in `tokens.json`, and let the guards compare it.
**Do** keep transitions 150–300ms on `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`; real objects decelerate smoothly.
**Do** mark AI-generated fields with the EU "AI GENERATED" provenance treatment on the label, and open the lede on an ink rule.
**Do** mix colors `in oklab`, derive primary variants from the seed, and run `npm run check:tokens` before trusting any token name.
**Do** test any new font against `ḥ ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ ʿ ā ī ū` before adopting it.
**Do** give every interactive element a visible focus state — `--focus-outline` first — and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** use warm cream or parchment surfaces — wrong register ("manuscript museum brochure").
**Don't** add atmospheric gradients, gradient bars, glassmorphism (outside the sticky header), or colored side-stripes.
**Don't** fill category badges or color `h2`s in primary — category is a dot, primary is an accent.
**Don't** use cold blue-gray dark surfaces — dark mode is warm ("lamplit"), hue ~70–80.
**Don't** box result rows, filter bars, linked-resource lists, or the AI lede into cards.
**Don't** replace an outline focus indicator with the `--ring-focus` halo for convenience, and never with `outline: none` alone.
**Don't** use bouncing/elastic easing or hover-triggered hero animations (the one-time Ken Burns settle is the sanctioned exception).
**Don't** pair Besley with `tabular-nums` (broken tnum zero) or track it tighter than -0.01em.
